title: Personal Account Dealing
summary: The rules on staff dealing for themselves and connected persons, why pre-clearance and holding periods exist, and how to avoid conflicts and front running.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The rules on staff dealing for themselves and connected persons, why pre-clearance and holding periods exist, and how to avoid conflicts and front running.
Learning Objectives: Explain the purpose and scope of the firm's personal account dealing policy
Apply pre-clearance, holding period and reporting requirements
Recognise dealing that creates conflicts of interest or market abuse risk
Syllabus: Accounts, instruments and connected persons covered by the rules
Pre-clearance, restricted lists, holding periods and disclosure
Front running, derivatives, crypto-assets and other grey areas
Monitoring, breaches and what happens when things go wrong
Intended Audience: All staff in regulated firms, including those outside trading and investment roles who may come across inside information
Front-office, research, operations, technology, marketing, HR and executive support staff
Line managers responsible for approving personal dealing, gifts and communications in their teams
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior knowledge of markets or regulation is required. The programme is relevant to all staff, not only those in trading or investment roles.
Core Reading: IOSCO (2017), Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation
IOSCO (2003), Insider Trading: How Jurisdictions Regulate It
FSB (2018), Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors
